ageing_relevance.rationale: About 10% of B2M papers concern ageing, and it is a GrimAge component protein. MR was not tested and Open Targets lists no ageing-disease associations, so causal evidence is missing.

evidence.value: not tested: no cis instruments (p < 5e-8 within 1 Mb of the gene; 1 genome-wide). Untested is not a null result.

One of seven plasma proteins whose DNA-methylation surrogates make up the GrimAge clock. Part 1 of this project: the GrimAge clock as a whole was +4.3 years older in schizophrenia, a difference that disappeared after adjusting for a methylation smoking score; this protein's own surrogate was not tested. Surrogates are methylation estimates, not measured protein levels. Shirai et al. 2024 (7-cohort meta-analysis): this protein's DNAm surrogate was higher in schizophrenia or first-episode psychosis in a model adjusted for age, sex and DNAm smoking pack-years.

background_knowledge: Circulating B2M is reported to rise with age and is described in the literature as a pro-ageing factor, for example in cognition studies in mice.
The Shirai finding concerns the DNAm surrogate, not measured protein.

mechanism.rationale: B2M is well characterised as the MHC class I light chain. Its causal link to ageing and the direction of modulation are unclear because there is no MR.

evidence.value: Component of the class I major histocompatibility complex (MHC). Involved in the presentation of peptide antigens to the immune system.

background_knowledge: B2M forms amyloid in dialysis-related amyloidosis.

tractability.rationale: Small-molecule evidence (structure with ligand, high-quality pocket) and antibody evidence (secreted and cell-surface localisation) exist. No approved-drug precedence is listed.

safety.rationale: No liabilities are listed, but absence of data is not evidence of safety. B2M is essential for MHC class I, and loss causes MHC class I deficiency, so inhibition could impair immunity.
background_knowledge: B2M loss impairs MHC class I antigen presentation and CD8 T-cell function.

clinical_precedence.rationale: No drugs are listed for B2M.

assessment.summary: B2M is the MHC class I light chain and a secreted plasma protein. It is one of the GrimAge component proteins, and about 10% of its literature concerns ageing. MR could not be run because there are no cis instruments, and Open Targets lists no ageing-disease associations. Its tractability is moderate (small-molecule and antibody evidence). No drugs are listed, and no safety liabilities are listed, but its immune role warrants caution. The direction of modulation is unclear, and I recommend we consider it, with the caveat that the causal evidence is missing.
key_uncertainties: No MR of measured B2M on lifespan, frailty or GrimAge acceleration; a non-cis instrument or other causal evidence would help.
Whether lowering circulating B2M, rather than cell-surface B2M, is safe and slows ageing.
The Shirai finding concerns the DNAm surrogate in schizophrenia, not the measured protein.
source_conflicts: Literature has 3025 ageing papers (share 0.1015), yet Open Targets lists no ageing disease associations (n_ageing 0). I treated the literature as indicating interest, not causal evidence.
Tractability lists small-molecule and antibody evidence, but the clinical candidates list is empty. I relied on the clinical list for precedence.
